1) Difficulties

During the scraping process for government documents from GovInfo.gov, I encountered several challenges.
The GovInfo site did not provide options to download search results in CSV or JSON formats directly from the search page. This broke the expected workflow in the assignment, which relies on metadata files to identify and download documents programmatically.
Thus, I had to manually download PDF files. This made the process time-consuming and error-prone.
Sample metadata from GitHub was outdated and did not match the documents I downloaded. Because of this, matching file names to metadata for analysis failed, which limited my ability to annotate or summarize the documents meaningfully.

2) How useable the scraped data?

Even though I was able to download 10 recent documents related to the Foreign Relations Committee, the data was in PDF format, which is difficult to process without extracting the text. The lack of metadata information (such as titles, dates, and summaries) made it difficult to filter, organize, or analyze the documents systematically.
Overall, the scraped data is partially usable but not ideal for structured analysis without additional manual processing.


3) How to improve?
Even if the website do not provide a CSV or JSON download, I can build a simple metadata table in R. Use file names, inferred dates, and keywords extracted from the text to organize and annotate the documents.

title: EPPS6356 - Assignment01
text:
Article
Kawashita, I., Baptista, A. A., Soares, D., & Andrade, M. (2024). Open government data use: The Brazilian states and federal district cases. Plos one, 19(3), e0298157.



In general, the article has clear graphs that effectively present statistical information from the survey and interviews. Personally, I do not prefer vivid colors such as red, yellow, and green, but the charts are clear enough to recognize the differences. However, the visualization of the research design needs improvement.




Research Design



The Phase 1 and Phase 2 titles at the top should include “Survey” and “Interview” labels rather than mentioning them inside the boxes or at the top of the research design.

The process shows “Literature Review” → “Questionnaire, Data Collection and Analysis” → “Interviews, Data Collection and Analysis” → “Combined Analysis of Results” → “Conclusion” → “Q1, Q2, and Q3.” I do not understand why the research questions appear after the conclusion.

The research design does not describe what the authors want to analyze through the survey and interviews. It does not include the variables or elements targeted by the authors. It looks more like a description of their working process rather than a research design.
